messages:
Priya S.: customer reporting streaming responses getting cut off after ~35s, partial JSON blob then connection closes. they see this from browser and from their app. (reported via support ticket)
Sam L.: do we know if customer is behind Cloudflare / ALB / nginx in front of us?
Priya S.: yes — they sit behind Cloudflare (proxy) which talks to an ALB -> nginx -> our service. customer says it works sometimes, but most of the time the stream stops around 30-40s. they pasted snippet from their client logs: `fetch` promise resolves with status 200 then body stream ends early.
Jorge R.: common culprits: ALB idle timeout, Cloudflare buffering, nginx proxy_buffering or proxy_read_timeout. any response headers from us when it dies? request-id?
Priya S.: they included X-Request-ID: r-9a7c. also saw intermittent `502` in ALB target health logs right around the disconnects.
Nadia P.: can we get them to run a few quick reproductions so we have tcpdump/curl traces? ask for `curl -v -N` to avoid local buffering and show chunk boundaries.
Priya S.: asked for that, customer returned a curl session dump: ```
> curl -v -N 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?req=abc' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< connection: keep-alive
data: {"text":"Hello"}\n\n
data: {"text":"Wor"\n# connection then RST from upstream
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.example left intact
```
Sam L.: interesting — last chunk `{"text":"Wor"` (truncated). suggests upstream closed mid-chunk. ALB logs show target 10.x.x.x returning 504 occasionally? that would be ALB idle/timeouts or target closed socket.
infra-bot: (automated) collected ALB logs for r-9a7c — 504, backend_connection_time ~ 61s
Jorge R.: backend_connection_time 61s -> sounds like ALB idle/body timeout. ALB default idle is 60s. If our streaming has periods with no bytes for >60s, ALB will close.
Nadia P.: but customer says it cuts ~35s, not 61s. Cloudflare can also give 524 (timeout) or buffer small chunks until threshold then flush. Cloudflare default proxy timeout is 100s, but CF can close earlier if origin pool issues.
Priya S.: customer also used their mobile app behind flaky cellular and saw same behaviour without Cloudflare. they ran a direct test to our origin (bypassing CF) and saw disconnects at ~34s, with nginx logs showing `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream`.
Sam L.: nginx error strongly points to upstream (our service) closing socket. Do we have our runtime logs for that request ID? any OOM/worker restart?
Jorge R.: checked runtime — no OOMs. But I see one of the inference workers reporting `keepalive timeout: client did not read from socket` then closed. There's code that aggressively kills idle connections after 30s if client not reading.
Nadia P.: ah, that matches ~30-35s. Could be our runtime's keepalive/idle detection interacting badly with ALB keepalives. If our runtime expects the client to aggressively read and it doesn't, it may close.
Priya S.: repro steps we sent to customer to gather more data:
  1) curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Connection: keep-alive' --limit-rate 1 https://<endpoint>
  2) tcpdump -w out.pcap host api.redwood.example and upload
  3) capture nginx error/access lines and ALB logs for the same timestamps
Please also run a direct bypass of Cloudflare (hosts file) if possible.
Sam L.: mitigation ideas for short-term: set nginx config `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s;` and in ALB increase idle timeout to 400s. Also on our service side, relax keepalive-to-client timeout to 120s.
Jorge R.: code-level fix: change the runtime so it sends periodic 1-2 byte heartbeat chunks (`:\n` SSE comment) every 20s when there is no real token output. SSE heartbeat is a proven pattern for intermediaries.
Nadia P.: also advise customer to disable Cloudflare features that buffer (e.g., Rocket Loader / Workers that modify responses) and ensure `Origin` keepalive is enabled. If they must keep CF, we can recommend `Cache-Control: no-transform` and ensure chunk sizes exceed CF's min buffer.
Priya S.: customer ran with `proxy_buffering off` and a runtime change to send `:heartbeat\n\n` every 15s — they reported significant improvement, no disconnects after 12 test minutes. We'll propose a durable fix on our side to add heartbeat by default for streaming endpoints.
customer-rep: customer very thankful, asked for a doc/KB to prevent this in future.
Sam L.: assign to eng-runtime to add optional heartbeat, and to eng-platform to publish recommended reverse-proxy config (ALB/NGINX/Cloudflare) in docs. tagging @eng-runtime @eng-platform.
Priya S.: next actions:
  - eng-runtime: add `sse_heartbeat_interval` config + fallback to send `:heartbeat` comments
  - eng-platform: docs page with ALB idle, nginx proxy_read/_send_timeout, `proxy_buffering off`, Cloudflare notes
  - support: collect a few more customer tcpdumps for final verification
Nadia P.: I'll create the GH issue for runtime and link this thread. :thumbsup:
Priya S.: closing loop with customer tomorrow after eng changes. thanks everyone. :heart:
